Its purpose is to ensure that:
the ZX-UX host compiler rcc can implement the C48 language without inventing missing language rules;
an independent host-based C48 compiler or interpreter can implement the same language;
a canonical C48 source file can be compiled by ZX-UX sdk/rcc to an SSX1 executable without source changes, subject to documented language/runtime resource limits;
C48 behavior does not depend on the behavior of a host ISO C compiler;
unsupported C features fail explicitly rather than acquiring accidental implementation-specific behavior.

requirements.section_title: 96. Grammar freeze versus runtime API freeze
requirements.text_prefix: The word const remains a reserved-but-unsupported C48 type modifier. Public declarations are those in sdk/include/c48.h, not inferred older architecture pseudocode.
Illustrative assembly/host interfaces may use modern-C const notation to describe read-only data. C48 Rev 0.11 itself does not accept const as a source type modifier.
The compiler MUST NOT acquire unsupported const semantics merely by importing a host header; only C48-compatible prototypes in sdk/include/c48.h form the current public runtime API.
This distinction also applies to every other modern-C spelling that appears only in explanatory host/pseudocode and is absent from the frozen C48 language.

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: The following cases close semantic gaps that can otherwise make Windows and native C48 disagree:

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: `char c = 1; c << 8` uses the 8-bit low-three-bit shift count and produces a `char`-typed shift result;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: `int i = 1; i << 16` uses the 16-bit low-four-bit shift count;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: bare `-32768` is distinguished from `(int)0x8000u`;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: `sizeof(array)` sees the whole array while `&array` is rejected;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: `argv[1][0]` succeeds while `1[argv]` is rejected;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: `i = i++` follows Section-55 left-to-right/address-then-RHS assignment order deterministically;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: fall-through from a non-void function takes the Section-69 status-1 runtime-error path;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: every compiler-generated floating numeric failure with no language error return takes the Section-53 status-1 runtime-error path;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: quoted includes use current host-source logical text and may include the built-in <c48.h> under the strict language include rules; obsolete kernel object-storage tags are not relevant;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: Equivalent canonical source bytes must compile to semantically equivalent SSO1/SSX1 results through the current host toolchain; legacy RAW/PACKED ZX-UX object storage is not a host source format.

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: `short`/`int`/pointer byte representation is little-endian and all-zero BSS yields integer zero, null pointer, and floating zero;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: pointer equality compares exact 16-bit logical address bits and relational comparison rejects incompatible/void pointer types;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: unsigned division/remainder and negative masked shift counts follow Sections 45-46;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: float-to-char conversion uses unsigned 16-bit conversion then low-eight-bit narrowing, while a negative value fails conversion;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: a float parameter remains pass-by-value even when the current ABI passes a pointer to its five-byte value;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: an 8-bit function result is returned in HL with H=0 and follows normal C48 promotion rules;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: normal return from `main` maps its `int` result to the low eight process-status bits;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: successful rcc returns status 0 and reports compiler failures on stderr;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: rebuilding identical input with the same checked sdk/rcc toolchain must produce repeatable SSO1/SSX1 bytes under a controlled environment;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: an empty/all-comment translation unit is accepted by the language parser; generating an executable without main is a separate linker failure;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: a compatible `main` prototype may precede its definition without a storage-class specifier, while a file-scope object named `main` is rejected;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: automatic initialized locals are reinitialized on every block activation and uninitialized locals retain unspecified bits;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: pure constant expressions exercise arithmetic casts and float comparisons without host-precision drift;

requirements.section_title: Appendix C. Additional Mandatory Cross-Compiler Conformance Cases
requirements.text_prefix: diagnostic tests cover current rcc stderr/error status, source positions when provided, and proper rejection of each required invalid C48 construct.
